summary:
We developed The Silent Witnesses of the Moon and Mars, an illustrated 7-page digital children's storybook created on Canva. Our story brings NASA's left-behind lunar and Martian spacecraft—including the Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle, ALSEP instruments, Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, and InSight—to life as courageous pioneers rather than forgotten space debris.
This project directly addresses the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge by transforming complex historical mission data from NASA Science into an accessible, emotionally engaging narrative for young learners. Instead of viewing inactive rovers and landers as old metal, readers discover how these machines served as historical time capsules, detected moonquakes and marsquakes, and uncovered clues about ancient water on Mars.
Preserving space history is vital because understanding the machines that paved the way inspires future generations of explorers, scientists, and engineers to stay curious and continue humanity's journey beyond Earth.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:
The Silent Witnesses of the Moon and Mars is a 7-page digital children's storybook designed to teach young readers about the spacecraft humanity left behind on the Moon and Mars. Structured into short, illustrated chapters, the book guides students through the journeys of the Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle, ALSEP lunar instruments, Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, and the InSight lander.
Benefits & Intended Impact:
Technical mission reports can feel intimidating for young students. By turning real NASA mission histories into an approachable bedtime-style story, our project builds emotional connection, sparks curiosity in STEM, and reframes inactive spacecraft as valuable historical time capsules rather than space junk.
Tools & Software Used:
We used NASA Science (science.nasa.gov) mission archives for historical accuracy and Canva to design, layout, and illustrate the 7-page presentation deck.
Creativity & Team Considerations:
Instead of presenting raw dates and technical specs, we gave each rover and lander a distinct story arc—highlighting how ALSEP listened to moonquakes, how Spirit and Opportunity searched for ancient water, and how InSight measured marsquakes. We prioritized clear typography, high-contrast visuals, and age-appropriate storytelling so children can read it easily on any screen.
